summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Satoru Noriyama studied under Eshō Mikogami (attested 1996). Noriyama held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima studied Buddhist studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and later served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan under Takao Kagawa, Shozen Kumoi, and Luis Oscar Gómez. He taught at Bukkyo University, Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College, and Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Satoshi Kono earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, Satoshi Naiki earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he later served as Assistant Professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

Satya Swarup Misra worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University (~1978–1995).

Satya Vrat Shastri was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Punjabi University and Banaras Hindu University. He held academic posts at the University of Delhi (~1961–1995) and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He held posts at the University of Dhaka, University of Calcutta, and Visva-Bharati University, serving as Vice-chancellor (~1956–1958).

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under U Paññāvanta and Mahasi Sayadaw. He held leadership roles at Mahāvijjodaya Chaung Monastery, Atithokdayone Pali University, Dhammananda Vihara, and as Chancellor of International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (~1999–2005).
Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Toyo University under doctoral supervisor Shinobu Yamaguchi and committee member Shogo Watanabe.

Scott A. Mitchell earned a PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne. A scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies, he became a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).
Scott Dalby, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and served as a lecturer at Amsterdam University College (attested 2014).

Scott Pacey earned a doctorate from Australian National University in 2011. Working in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, he held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and lectured at the University of Manchester (attested 2014).

Sean D. Gaffney, specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski. He also studied under Philip Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held an affiliation with SOAS.
See Mui Yian studied Buddhist studies at the University of Hong Kong, earning a PhD under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).
Seema Alavi is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991). She held academic posts at the University of Delhi (~2003–2020) and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seigai Omura worked in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) and served as a professor at Tokyo School of Fine Arts (~1898–1927).
Seiichi Mizuno specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1927–1930) and later served as a professor there (~1949–1968).
Seiichiro Ono studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1917). Active in Buddhist studies and other fields, he held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University.

Seiji Kimura, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
